new-delhi.name: New Delhi
new-delhi.famousLandmark: Jama Masjid – one of the largest mosques in India
new-delhi.insights: New Delhi, the heart of India, is home to one of the country's most historic Muslim communities. The Walled City (Shahjahanabad), built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in the 17th century, remains a crown jewel of Islamic heritage in South Asia. The towering Jama Masjid — constructed between 1644 and 1656 — can accommodate over 25,000 worshippers and stands as a powerful symbol of Delhi's Islamic legacy. From Lodi Garden's 15th-century tombs to Humayun's Tomb and Nizamuddin Dargah, the city breathes centuries of Sufi tradition and Mughal grandeur.
facts: The Jama Masjid in Old Delhi was commissioned by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan and completed in 1656 — it can hold over 25,000 worshippers.
Nizamuddin Dargah, the shrine of Sufi saint Nizamuddin Auliya, draws thousands of devotees every week for Qawwali gatherings.
Delhi has over 1,300 mosques, with the highest concentration in the Walled City area of Shahjahanabad.
The Mehrauli Archaeological Park contains over 100 medieval monuments, many of Islamic origin, including the iconic Qutub Minar.
During Ramadan, markets like Urdu Bazaar and Matia Mahal in Old Delhi come alive with special iftar spreads and nocturnal cultural celebrations.
new-delhi.ramadanNote: During Ramadan, the lanes around Jama Masjid and Nizamuddin Auliya's dargah are especially vibrant — local restaurants offer special iftar menus and Qawwali nights are held after Taraweeh prayer.

faqItems.q: What method is used for New Delhi prayer time calculations?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the University of Islamic Sciences (Karachi) method with Fajr and Isha angles of 18°, widely accepted across the Indian subcontinent.

faqItems.q: Are these timings valid for Noida and Gurgaon?
faqItems.a: Yes, based on the coordinates (28.6139° N, 77.2090° E), these timings are accurate for the entire Delhi NCR region including Noida, Gurgaon, and Ghaziabad with less than 60 seconds variation.

faqItems.q: When does Ramadan 2026 start in New Delhi?
faqItems.a: Ramadan 2026 is expected to begin on February 19, 2026, in New Delhi, subject to moon sighting confirmation.

mumbai.name: Mumbai
mumbai.famousLandmark: Haji Ali Dargah – iconic mosque-shrine on a tidal islet
mumbai.insights: Mumbai is home to one of India's largest and most diverse urban Muslim communities, comprising roughly 19% of the city's population. The iconic Haji Ali Dargah, perched on a small islet off Worli, is one of the most-visited Muslim shrines in the country. From the historic Minara Masjid in Bhendi Bazaar to the grand Jama Masjid near Crawford Market, Mumbai's Islamic heritage stretches across centuries. The city's Muslim artisans, traders, and scholars have been integral to its identity since the Mughal and Portuguese eras.
facts: The Haji Ali Dargah, built in 1431, is connected to the mainland by a 500-metre causeway that gets submerged at high tide.
Bhendi Bazaar in South Mumbai is a centuries-old Muslim cultural enclave and one of the city's most vibrant food markets during Ramadan.
Mumbai's Bohri Muslim community operates a unique religious infrastructure including exclusive mosques and social welfare networks.
The Mohammad Ali Road area becomes one of India's most famous Ramadan food streets, drawing thousands nightly for Raan, Nalli Nihari, and Malpua.
Mumbai has the largest concentration of Muslims in any Indian city by absolute numbers, with nearly 4 million adherents.
mumbai.ramadanNote: Mohammad Ali Road in Mumbai transforms into a legendary iftar destination during Ramadan — the street food here is considered some of the best in South Asia.

faqItems.q: What calculation method is used for Mumbai prayer times?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the University of Islamic Sciences (Karachi) method for Mumbai, with a Fajr angle of 18° and Isha angle of 18°.

faqItems.q: Are these timings valid for Thane and Navi Mumbai?
faqItems.a: These timings are based on central Mumbai coordinates (19.0760° N, 72.8777° E). For Thane or Navi Mumbai, there may be a 1–3 minute difference due to geographical distance.

faqItems.q: When is Ramadan 2026 Iftar in Mumbai?
faqItems.a: Mumbai's Iftar (Maghrib) time shifts slightly later than New Delhi due to its more southerly and westerly location. Check today's live timing card for an accurate time.

bangalore.name: Bangalore
bangalore.famousLandmark: Jamia Masjid – the largest mosque in Bangalore
bangalore.insights: Bangalore, India's Silicon Valley, has a Muslim population that blends centuries of Deccani culture with a modern, cosmopolitan identity. The city's Shivajinagar and Cox Town neighbourhoods are home to vibrant Muslim communities, the city's most historic mosques, and bustling bazaars with a rich South Indian Muslim culinary tradition. Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace, a fine example of Indo-Islamic architecture, stands as a reminder of the city's deep Muslim history under the Mysore Sultanate.
facts: Tipu Sultan, the Tiger of Mysore, ruled Bangalore as part of his Sultanate and built several mosques, including the Idgah Masjid.
Shivajinagar is Bangalore's primary Muslim commercial and cultural hub, featuring the city's central mosque, gold markets, and spice bazaars.
The Bangalore biryani style, a lighter Deccani variant, is a culinary contribution of the local Muslim community.
Bangalore has over 300 registered mosques, with the Jamia Masjid being the most prominent for Friday congregations.
Karnataka has a significant Muslim minority of around 13%, making Bangalore a major centre of Islamic culture in South India.
bangalore.ramadanNote: During Ramadan, the Nixon area and Shivajinagar fill with iftar stalls serving Haleem, Biryani, and sweet shops open late into the night.

faqItems.q: What calculation method is used for Bangalore prayer times?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the University of Islamic Sciences (Karachi) method for Bangalore, with Fajr and Isha angles of 18°.

faqItems.q: Is the Fajr time in Bangalore earlier or later than Delhi?
faqItems.a: Bangalore is further south and close to the same longitude as Delhi. Fajr time in Bangalore is typically 30–60 minutes later than New Delhi due to the time zone being the same (IST) but the sun rising differently.

faqItems.q: When does Ramadan 2026 begin in Bangalore?
faqItems.a: Ramadan 2026 is expected to begin around February 19, 2026, in Bangalore, subject to moon sighting confirmation.

hyderabad.name: Hyderabad
hyderabad.famousLandmark: Mecca Masjid – one of the oldest and largest mosques in India
hyderabad.insights: Hyderabad, the City of Pearls, carries the richest Islamic cultural legacy in Deccan India. Founded by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah in 1591, the city flourished under the Nizams and became a global centre of Urdu literature, Islamic jurisprudence, and refined culture. The Mecca Masjid — one of the largest mosques in Asia — and the iconic Charminar are symbols of this grand heritage. Today, Old Hyderabad remains one of the most architecturally and culturally Muslim cities in South India.
facts: Mecca Masjid, built by the Qutb Shahi dynasty and completed by Aurangzeb in 1694, can accommodate up to 10,000 worshippers at once.
The Charminar, built in 1591, was constructed by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah to mark the location where a plague epidemic ended.
Hyderabad's Dum Biryani is world-famous and was perfected in the royal kitchens of the Nizam.
The Nizams of Hyderabad were among the wealthiest rulers in the world and were known for generous endowments to Islamic institutions.
Hyderabad is home to some of India's finest Urdu newspapers and hosts an international Urdu festival every year.
hyderabad.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Hyderabad is a grand affair — the lanes of the Charminar and Laad Bazaar are lit up, Haleem is prepared in massive quantities, and the Mecca Masjid holds some of the most moving Taraweeh prayers in the country.

faqItems.q: Which method is used for Hyderabad Namaz timings?
faqItems.a: We use the University of Islamic Sciences (Karachi) method for Hyderabad, with a Fajr angle of 18° and Isha angle of 18°.

faqItems.q: What is the significance of the Mecca Masjid for local prayer?
faqItems.a: The Mecca Masjid is the primary Friday congregational mosque for Hyderabad's Muslim community and has been so for over 300 years. Bricks from Mecca were used in its central arch, hence the name.

faqItems.q: When does Ramadan 2026 start in Hyderabad?
faqItems.a: Ramadan 2026 is expected to begin on February 19, 2026, in Hyderabad, subject to official moon sighting.

chennai.name: Chennai
chennai.famousLandmark: Wallajah Big Mosque (Nawab's Mosque) in Triplicane
chennai.insights: Chennai has a distinct and ancient Muslim heritage. The Tamil Muslims, known locally as Labbai, trace their roots to Arab traders who came to the Coromandel Coast over a thousand years ago. The Wallajah Mosque in Triplicane, built in 1795, is one of South India's most revered mosques. Chennai's Muslim community plays a vital role in the city's trade, cuisine, and cultural fabric — from the fragrant biryani of Triplicane to the Sufi shrines along the coast.
facts: Arab traders arrived on the Tamil Nadu coast as early as the 7th century CE, establishing one of the oldest Muslim communities in India.
The Wallajah Big Mosque in Triplicane was built by Nawab Muhammad Ali Khan Wallajah in 1795 and remains a major spiritual centre.
The tomb of the Islamic scholar Shaikh Muhammad Yusuf, near Royapuram, is a significant pilgrimage site for local Muslims.
Tamil Nadu's unique Dakhni cuisine, particularly the Ambur and Arcot styles of Biryani, are beloved across India.
Chennai's Triplicane and Royapuram areas have some of the oldest mosques in South India, many dating to the 17th and 18th centuries.
chennai.ramadanNote: During Ramadan, Chennai's Triplicane area buzzes with festivity — local khaana shops serve elaborate iftar spreads and the Wallajah Mosque holds a large communal iftar for thousands.

faqItems.q: What calculation method is used for Chennai prayer times?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the University of Islamic Sciences (Karachi) method for Chennai, with Fajr and Isha angles of 18°.

faqItems.q: Is Fajr time in Chennai different from North India?
faqItems.a: Yes, because Chennai is further south and shares the same time zone (IST) as all of India, its Fajr time is typically around 20–40 minutes later than Delhi during winter months.

faqItems.q: When is Eid ul-Fitr 2026 in Chennai?
faqItems.a: Eid ul-Fitr 2026 is expected around March 20–21, 2026, subject to moon sighting. The Eid prayer is traditionally held at the Chepauk Stadium ground and the Wallajah Mosque.

kolkata.name: Kolkata
kolkata.famousLandmark: Nakhoda Mosque – the city's grand Friday mosque
kolkata.insights: Kolkata, the cultural capital of East India, has a long and layered Islamic heritage. The Nakhoda Mosque — a stunning red sandstone structure modelled on Akbar's tomb in Sikandra — is the city's principal mosque and can hold 10,000 worshippers. The Tipu Sultan Mosque (1832) and the historic mosques of central Kolkata bear witness to centuries of Muslim intellectual and artistic contribution to Bengal. Kolkata's Muslim community has been instrumental in shaping the city's literature, music, and culinary traditions.
facts: The Nakhoda Mosque, completed in 1926, was built by the Kutchi Memon community and modelled on Mughal architecture.
West Bengal has the second-highest Muslim population of any Indian state, with nearly 27% of the state being Muslim.
Kolkata's Mughlai cuisine — Kathi Rolls, Nargisi Kofta, and Rezala — was developed in Muslim kitchens and is now iconic globally.
The poet and Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore was deeply influenced by Baul and Sufi mysticism, reflecting in Bengal's unique composite culture.
Park Circus and Rajabazar are the main Muslim neighbourhoods of Kolkata, known for their vibrant Eid celebrations and Muharram processions.
kolkata.ramadanNote: During Ramadan, the Park Circus area and the lanes near Nakhoda Mosque host some of Kolkata's most popular iftar markets, famous for Haleem, Kebabs, Firni, and Shahi Tukda.

faqItems.q: What method is used for Kolkata prayer time calculations?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the University of Islamic Sciences (Karachi) method for Kolkata, with Fajr and Isha angles of 18°.

faqItems.q: Is sunrise earlier in Kolkata than the rest of India?
faqItems.a: Yes. Kolkata is one of the easternmost major Indian cities, so sun-based prayer times like Fajr and Maghrib occur earlier than in New Delhi or Mumbai despite all sharing the IST (UTC+5:30) timezone.

faqItems.q: What is the Eid ground in Kolkata?
faqItems.a: Eid prayers in Kolkata are traditionally held at the Red Road ground near the Victoria Memorial, one of the largest open-air Eid congregations in India.

lucknow.name: Lucknow
lucknow.famousLandmark: Asafi (Bara) Imambara – a magnificent Nawabi monument
lucknow.insights: Lucknow, the City of Nawabs, is one of the most refined centres of Urdu culture and Islamic civilisation in the world. Home to the Awadhi Nawabs who ruled in the 18th and 19th centuries, Lucknow developed the tehzeeb (etiquette), poetry, music, and cuisine that define Urdu cultural identity. The Hussainabad precinct, with the Bara Imambara, Chota Imambara, and Rumi Darwaza, is among South Asia's most spectacular examples of Indo-Islamic architecture. Lucknow's Shia Muslim community, one of the most prominent in the subcontinent, gives the city a particularly distinctive religious character.
facts: The Bara Imambara, built in 1784, contains the largest vaulted hall in the world built without the use of steel or wood beams.
Lucknow's Dum Pukht (slow-cooked) biryani and Galouti Kebabs were invented in the royal kitchens of the Nawabs and are now famous globally.
The Rumi Darwaza (1784), inspired by the Sublime Porte in Istanbul, is one of the most iconic gateways in India.
The Dargah-e-Hazrat Abbas is one of the most visited Shia shrines in India, especially during the month of Muharram.
Lucknow's Urdu literary tradition produced greats like Mir Anees, Mir Dard, and Dagh Dehlvi, whose works remain canonical in South Asian poetry.
lucknow.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Lucknow is as much a cultural event as a religious one — the bazaars of Aminabad and Hazratganj overflow with special iftar delicacies, Sheer Korma, Phirni, and handmade sherbet.

faqItems.q: What method is used for Lucknow prayer time calculations?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the University of Islamic Sciences (Karachi) method for Lucknow, with Fajr and Isha angles of 18°.

faqItems.q: Is Lucknow prayer time the same as New Delhi?
faqItems.a: Lucknow is slightly east of New Delhi (by ~3° longitude), so prayer times like Fajr and Maghrib occur about 10–12 minutes earlier than in New Delhi.

faqItems.q: Where is the main Eid prayer held in Lucknow?
faqItems.a: The main Eid prayers in Lucknow are traditionally held at the Eidgah grounds in Hussainabad and the Aishbagh Eidgah, drawing tens of thousands of worshippers.

jaipur.name: Jaipur
jaipur.famousLandmark: Atish Market Mosque and historic mosques in the Walled City
jaipur.insights: Jaipur, the Pink City, is known for its vibrant Rajput heritage — but its Muslim community has been equally central to the city's story. Muslim artisans, poets, and traders have shaped Jaipur's architecture, handicrafts, and trade networks for centuries. The city's Walled City area contains numerous historic mosques and tombs. From the Sunehri Kothi to the Idgah Mosque, and from gem-cutting workshops run by Muslim craftsmen to Persian-inspired architecture, Jaipur's Islamic fingerprint is visible at every turn.
facts: Jaipur's world-famous gemstone cutting and jewellery industry has historically been dominated by Muslim artisans from the Mughal era.
The city has the largest Eid congregation in Rajasthan, held annually at the Idgah grounds near Amer Fort.
Jaipur's Muslim community settled in large numbers during the Mughal period, and many of their descendants continue to live in the historic Walled City.
Rajasthan has unique Meo Muslim communities in the northeast, known for preserving pre-Islamic folk traditions alongside Islamic faith.
The Dargah of Hazrat Nizamuddin Chishti in Ajmer (nearby) draws millions from across India and the world, making Rajasthan a major Sufi pilgrimage hub.
jaipur.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Jaipur brings alive the Walled City's markets — the Johari Bazaar area hosts colourful iftar stalls and the local Shahi Tukda and Malpua are a must-try.

faqItems.q: What calculation method is used for Jaipur prayer times?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the University of Islamic Sciences (Karachi) method for Jaipur, with Fajr and Isha angles of 18°.

faqItems.q: Is Jaipur prayer time the same as New Delhi?
faqItems.a: Jaipur is about 2° west of New Delhi, so its prayer times are typically 8–10 minutes later than New Delhi for times like Fajr and Maghrib.

faqItems.q: Where is the famous Sufi shrine near Jaipur?
faqItems.a: The Ajmer Sharif Dargah, dedicated to Hazrat Moinuddin Chishti, is located about 130 km from Jaipur and is one of the most visited shrines in the Islamic world.

ahmedabad.name: Ahmedabad
ahmedabad.famousLandmark: Jama Masjid of Ahmedabad (1424) – a UNESCO World Heritage site
ahmedabad.insights: Ahmedabad, founded by Sultan Ahmad Shah I in 1411, bears one of the richest concentrations of Islamic architecture in South Asia. The old city — a UNESCO World Heritage Site — is filled with mosques, tombs, and step wells built by the Sultanate of Gujarat. The Jama Masjid, Sidi Saiyyed Mosque (famous for its intricate stone jali), and the Hutheesing Jain Temple collectively tell the story of Gujarat's pluralistic medieval identity. Ahmedabad's Muslim community today is diverse, including Sunni, Bohri, Ismaili, and other sects.
facts: The Sidi Saiyyed Mosque's intricately carved stone jali lattice windows (1573) are among the finest examples of Islamic stone carving in the world.
Ahmedabad's Jama Masjid (1424) was built by Ahmad Shah I and served as the royal mosque of the Gujarat Sultanate.
The Bohri (Dawoodi Bohra) Muslim community, headquartered in Mumbai but strongest in Gujarat, has deep roots in Ahmedabad's history.
The Roza of Ahmad Shah I and the Mahmud Begada tomb complex represent some of Gujarat's most exquisite Indo-Saracenic architecture.
Ahmedabad's old city has 26 religious precincts (pol) reflecting centuries of Hindu-Muslim coexistence in shared neighbourhoods.
ahmedabad.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Ahmedabad's old city is intensely spiritual — the Jama Masjid and surrounding alleyways host nightly iftar gatherings, and the famous Bohri mohalla prepares traditional Bohri cuisine.

faqItems.q: What method is used for Ahmedabad prayer times?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the University of Islamic Sciences (Karachi) method for Ahmedabad, with Fajr and Isha angles of 18°.

faqItems.q: Is Ahmedabad's Fajr time different from Mumbai?
faqItems.a: Ahmedabad is north of Mumbai and about 1° west, so its prayer times are very close to Mumbai's — typically within 3–5 minutes for most prayers.

faqItems.q: Is the Sidi Saiyyed Mosque open to non-Muslim visitors?
faqItems.a: Yes, the Sidi Saiyyed Mosque is open to all visitors outside of prayer times. Its jali windows are considered among the finest stone carvings in India and are a major heritage landmark.

srinagar.name: Srinagar
srinagar.famousLandmark: Hazratbal Shrine – houses a relic believed to be hair of the Prophet ﷺ
srinagar.insights: Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu & Kashmir, is India's most predominantly Muslim city and one of the most spiritually significant in the subcontinent. Islam reached Kashmir in the 14th century through the Sufi saint Mir Syed Ali Hamadani and became deeply embedded in the region's culture, weaving together Persian mysticism with Kashmiri identity. The Hazratbal Shrine on Dal Lake and the Jamia Masjid in the old city are the beating heart of Islamic life in the Valley. Kashmir's distinct form of Sufism — Rishi tradition — has shaped centuries of tolerance, devotion, and poetry.
facts: The Hazratbal Shrine houses a relic (Moi-e-Muqaddas) believed to be a hair of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ — it is one of the holiest sites for Muslims in South Asia.
Mir Syed Ali Hamadani (Shah-e-Hamadan) brought Islam to Kashmir in the 14th century and is credited with converting over 37,000 Kashmiris.
The Jamia Masjid of Srinagar, founded in 1394, was built in the Indo-Saracenic style with 378 wooden pillars and can hold 33,000 worshippers.
Kashmir's unique form of Muslim devotion — Sufiana Kalam (Sufi poetry set to classical music) — is a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.
Kashmiri embroidery (Kashida), papier-mâché, and walnut wood crafts have been practiced predominantly by Muslim artisans for centuries.
srinagar.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Srinagar is a time of extraordinary spiritual intensity — the Dal Lake shimmers with Hazratbal's lights, homes keep iftar tables open, and the Wazwan feast is prepared for communal breaking of fast.

faqItems.q: What method is used for Srinagar prayer time calculations?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the University of Islamic Sciences (Karachi) method for Srinagar. The city's northerly latitude (34°N) means Fajr and Isha angles can produce long twilight times, especially in summer.

faqItems.q: Does Srinagar have very long fasting hours in summer Ramadan?
faqItems.a: Yes. Because Srinagar is at a high latitude, summer Ramadan fasting hours can exceed 16–17 hours. In winter Ramadan (2026), fasting is around 12–13 hours, making it more manageable.

faqItems.q: What is the significance of the Hazratbal Shrine?
faqItems.a: Hazratbal Shrine houses a relic believed to be a hair of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. It is among the holiest sites in South Asian Islam, and large congregations gather there on Eid and other occasions.

jakarta.name: Jakarta
jakarta.famousLandmark: Istiqlal Mosque - the largest mosque in Southeast Asia
jakarta.insights: Jakarta is one of the world's largest Muslim-majority capitals. Istiqlal Mosque stands at the center of the city's Islamic life, hosting major congregations for Jumu'ah, Ramadan, and Eid. The city's diverse Muslim communities include Betawi, Javanese, Sundanese, Arab-Indonesian, and other traditions.
facts: Istiqlal Mosque in Central Jakarta is the largest mosque in Southeast Asia and can host over 100,000 worshippers.
Jakarta follows WIB (UTC+7), which makes local prayer windows different from Gulf and South Asian cities.
During Ramadan, many neighborhoods run free iftar programs (takjil) before Magrib prayer.
The city has thousands of mosques and musallas serving daily congregational prayer.
Islamic study circles and Quran recitation programs are widely active throughout the year.
jakarta.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Jakarta is marked by strong communal iftar culture, night prayers, and active mosque programs across all districts.

faqItems.q: What method is used for Jakarta Namaz timings on RuhVerse?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses AlAdhan calculations with method 3 for Jakarta coordinates, then renders daily timings for Fajr, Zohr, Asr, Magrib, and Isha.

faqItems.q: Are these timings valid for all of Greater Jakarta?
faqItems.a: These timings are centered on Jakarta coordinates. Nearby areas like Depok, Bekasi, and Tangerang may differ slightly by a few minutes.

faqItems.q: Do Ramadan and Eid dates vary in Jakarta?
faqItems.a: Yes. Ramadan and Eid are moon-sighting based, so official Indonesian announcements should be followed for final confirmation.

mecca.name: Mecca
mecca.famousLandmark: Masjid al-Haram – the holiest mosque in Islam
mecca.insights: Mecca is the spiritual heart of the Islamic world and the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. As home to the Kaaba at Masjid al-Haram, it is the focal point of the Qibla for Muslims worldwide. The city's history is the history of Islam itself, from the first revelations at Jabal al-Nour to the grand assemblies of the Hajj pilgrimage. Every brick and stone in Mecca tells a story of devotion spanning over 14 centuries.
facts: The Masjid al-Haram is the largest mosque in the world and can accommodate up to 4 million worshippers during Hajj.
The Kaaba, located in the center of the mosque, was traditionally rebuilt by Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and his son Isma'il (AS).
Mecca is home to the Well of Zamzam, which has provided water to millions of pilgrims for thousands of years.
The city's Clock Tower (Abraj Al-Bait) is one of the tallest buildings in the world and serves as a primary landmark for pilgrims.
Entrance to the sacred city of Mecca is exclusively reserved for Muslims as per Saudi Arabian law and Islamic tradition.
mecca.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Mecca is an unparalleled experience — the Masjid al-Haram never sleeps, with millions breaking fast together on the marble courtyards and performing Umrah throughout the night.

faqItems.q: What calculation method is used for Mecca prayer times?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Umm al-Qura University method, which is the official standard for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

faqItems.q: Are the timings valid for the entire city of Mecca?
faqItems.a: Yes, these timings are calculated for the center of Mecca. Due to the city's terrain, slight variations of less than a minute may occur in distant outskirts.

faqItems.q: When is the best time to perform Umrah during Ramadan?
faqItems.a: Following the Sunnah, performing Umrah during Ramadan is highly virtuous. Late-night sessions after Taraweeh or during Tahajjud are popular but can be very crowded.

medina.name: Medina
medina.insights: Medina, the 'Radiant City', served as the destination of the Hijrah and the cradle of the first Islamic state. It is uniquely beloved by Muslims as the city where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ lived, taught, and was ultimately laid to rest. The atmosphere in Medina is known for its profound tranquility (sakinah), centered around the Green Dome of the Prophet's Mosque and the historic sites of the Sahaba.
facts: Al-Masjid an-Nabawi was originally built by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself and has been expanded by Islamic rulers over centuries.
The mosque contains the Rawdah ash-Sharifah, an area believed to be a piece of Jannah (Paradise) on Earth.
Medina is home to the Quba Mosque, the first mosque ever built in Islam by the Prophet ﷺ upon his arrival.
The city was formerly known as Yathrib before being renamed Madinat al-Nabi (City of the Prophet).
The historic cemetery of Jannat al-Baqi contains the resting places of many of the Prophet's family members and early companions.
medina.ramadanNote: Medina's iftar is world-famous for its hospitality — the local residents (Ansar) continue the tradition of inviting pilgrims to share dates, yogurt, and bread in the mosque courtyards.

faqItems.q: Which method is used for Medina Namaz timings?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Umm al-Qura calculation method for all cities in Saudi Arabia, including Medina.

faqItems.q: How does Medina's prayer time compare to Mecca?
faqItems.a: Medina is north of Mecca, so prayer times typically occur a few minutes later than in Mecca, depending on the season.

faqItems.q: Is Al-Masjid an-Nabawi open 24/7 during Ramadan?
faqItems.a: Yes, during the holy month, the Prophet's Mosque remains open throughout the day and night for prayer, recitation, and Tahajjud.

riyadh.name: Riyadh
riyadh.famousLandmark: Al Rajhi Grand Mosque – a center of Islamic learning
riyadh.insights: Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia, is a city where modern skyscrapers stand alongside historic mud-brick forts. It is a major center of Islamic scholarship and home to some of the world's most impressive modern mosques. The city's history is deeply tied to the Diriyah region, where the first Saudi state was founded on the principles of Islamic revival.
facts: The Al Rajhi Grand Mosque is one of the largest and most architecturally stunning contemporary mosques in the capital.
Riyadh's Diriyah district is a UNESCO World Heritage site and the original home of the Saudi Royal family.
The Imam Turki bin Abdullah Mosque is a historic landmark in the city center where major religious gatherings are held.
Riyadh hosts some of the largest Islamic universities in the world, attracting students from across the globe.
The city was once a small oasis town and has transformed into a global metropolis of over 7 million people.
riyadh.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Riyadh is a time of vibrant evening activity — markets and restaurants stay open until Sahur, and the city's mosques are filled for nightly Taraweeh prayers.

faqItems.q: What method is used for Riyadh prayer time calculations?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Umm al-Qura University method for Riyadh, the standard for all official timings in the Kingdom.

faqItems.q: Is the prayer time in Riyadh different from the Eastern Province?
faqItems.a: Yes, Riyadh is in the central region; cities in the Eastern Province like Dammam see the sunrise and sunset earlier due to their eastern location.

faqItems.q: When does Tahajjud prayer start in Riyadh during the last 10 days of Ramadan?
faqItems.a: Tahajjud congregational prayers typically start in the major mosques of Riyadh after midnight, usually around 1:00 AM or 1:30 AM.

dubai.name: Dubai
dubai.famousLandmark: Jumeirah Mosque – an iconic example of Islamic architecture
dubai.insights: Dubai is a global crossroads that beautifully blends high-tech ambition with traditional Islamic values. The city's skyline is punctuated by hundreds of minarets, ranging from the historic mosques of Al Fahidi to the modern marvels of Jumeirah and the Blue Mosque. Dubai's vibrant Muslim community represents nearly every culture on Earth, making its Eid and Ramadan celebrations exceptionally diverse and festive.
facts: The Jumeirah Mosque is one of the most photographed mosques in Dubai and is uniquely open to visitors of all faiths for cultural exchange.
Dubai's Al Farooq Omar Bin Al Khattab Mosque is modeled after the Blue Mosque in Istanbul and is a major center for community activities.
The call to prayer (Adhan) is synchronized across the city's 2,000+ mosques through a central system.
Dubai's historic district, Al Fahidi, contains some of the oldest mosques in the UAE, built with traditional wind-tower architecture.
The city hosts the Dubai International Holy Quran Award (DIHQA) annually, drawing participants from around the world.
dubai.ramadanNote: During Ramadan, Dubai's 'Ramadan Tents' offer a luxury iftar experience, while the city's charities distribute thousands of meals to the community in the spirit of giving.

faqItems.q: What calculation method is used for Dubai prayer times?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Umm al-Qura method for Dubai, which is widely adopted across the Gulf region.

faqItems.q: Are these timings valid for Hatta?
faqItems.a: Hatta is about 130km from Dubai city center; its prayer times typically differ by 1–2 minutes due to its more easterly location.

faqItems.q: When is the Eid Al-Fitr prayer in Dubai?
faqItems.a: Eid prayers are traditionally held in the city's major Eidgahs (musallas) and mosques around 15–20 minutes after sunrise.

karachi.name: Karachi
karachi.famousLandmark: Mazar-e-Quaid – the mausoleum of Pakistan's founder
karachi.insights: Karachi, the City of Lights, is a massive metropolis and a melting pot of Islamic cultures from across South Asia. Home to the towering Tooba Mosque (Gol Masjid) and the historic mosques of the Old City, Karachi's spiritual life is as vibrant as its economy. The city's residents are known for their resilience and deep-rooted faith, with thousands of mosques serving as community hubs in every district from Clifton to North Nazimabad.
facts: Masjid-e-Tooba, known as the Gol Masjid, is the largest single-domed mosque in the world, built with pure white marble.
Karachi is home to the shrine of Abdullah Shah Ghazi, one of the most revered Sufi saints in Pakistan.
The Jamia Tur Rasheed in Karachi is one of the largest Islamic educational institutions in the region.
During the month of Rabi-ul-Awwal, Karachi's streets are transformed with stunning illuminations to celebrate Eid Milad-un-Nabi.
Karachi's Burns Road and Husainabad are legendary for their iftar food markets during the holy month of Ramadan.
karachi.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Karachi is legendary for its nocturnal life — markets stay open until breakfast, and the smell of fresh pakoras and jalebis fills the air at sunset.

faqItems.q: What method is used for Karachi prayer time calculations?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the University of Islamic Sciences (Karachi) method, which originated right here in this city, with Fajr and Isha at 18°.

faqItems.q: Are these timings accurate for Bahria Town Karachi?
faqItems.a: Bahria Town is on the outskirts; prayer times may vary by 1–2 minutes from the city center coordinates used here.

faqItems.q: When does the moon-sighting committee meet in Karachi?
faqItems.a: The Central Ruet-e-Hilal Committee often holds its primary sessions at the Met Office in Karachi to determine the start of Ramadan and Eid.

lahore.name: Lahore
lahore.famousLandmark: Badshahi Mosque – a masterpiece of Mughal architecture
lahore.insights: Lahore, the cultural soul of Pakistan, holds some of the most magnificent Islamic heritage in the world. From the grand Badshahi Mosque built by Aurangzeb to the intricate tile-work of the Wazir Khan Mosque, Lahore's Mughal past is visible in every corner of the Walled City. The city is also a major center for Sufism, with the Data Darbar shrine drawing millions of devotees throughout the year.
facts: The Badshahi Mosque was the largest mosque in the world for over 300 years and is a prime example of Mughal floral art.
Data Darbar is the largest Sufi shrine in South Asia, dedicated to the 11th-century saint Abul Hassan Ali Hajvery (RA).
Lahore's Grand Jamia Mosque in Bahria Town is one of the largest contemporary mosques, featuring a blend of Mughal and modern styles.
The Wazir Khan Mosque is known locally as the 'shining jewel of Lahore' for its extraordinary fresco and tile work.
Lahore's Minar-e-Pakistan marks the spot where the resolution to create a separate Muslim state was passed in 1940.
lahore.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Lahore is famous for its Sehri and Iftar at the Food Street near Badshahi Mosque, where the view of the illuminated minarets is breathtaking.

faqItems.q: What calculation method is used for Lahore prayer times?
faqItems.a: We use the University of Islamic Sciences (Karachi) method for Lahore, with the standard 18° angle for Fajr and Isha.

faqItems.q: How do Lahore's timings differ from Islamabad?
faqItems.a: Lahore is south and slightly east of Islamabad, so prayer times like Fajr and Maghrib usually occur a few minutes earlier than in the capital.

faqItems.q: Where is the main Eid congregational prayer held in Lahore?
faqItems.a: The largest Eid prayers are held at the Badshahi Mosque and the massive Eidgah grounds near the city center.

dhaka.name: Dhaka
dhaka.famousLandmark: Baitul Mukarram – the National Mosque of Bangladesh
dhaka.insights: Dhaka, often called the 'City of Mosques', has a history of Islamic architecture that dates back to the Mughal era. The city is home to thousands of mosques, from the historic Star Mosque (Tara Masjid) with its intricate motifs to the massive Baitul Mukarram National Mosque. Dhaka's Muslim community is known for its intense devotion, especially during the annual Bishwa Ijtema, one of the largest Islamic gatherings in the world.
facts: Baitul Mukarram National Mosque was designed in the shape of the Kaaba in Mecca and can hold over 40,000 worshippers.
Dhaka is the site of the Bishwa Ijtema, an annual three-day congregation that is considered the second-largest Muslim gathering after Hajj.
The Star Mosque in Old Dhaka is a 19th-century marvel decorated with hundreds of blue stars made from broken porcelain.
The Hussaini Dalan, built in the 17th century, is the primary center for the city's Shia community during Muharram.
Dhaka's historic Chawkbazar is famous for its 'Iftar Bazar', where unique traditional food like 'Boro Baper Polay Khay' is sold.
dhaka.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Dhaka transforms the city's markets — Old Dhaka's Chawkbazar becomes a bustling hub for iftar hunters, with stalls overflowing with kebabs and sweets.

faqItems.q: What method is used for Dhaka prayer time calculations?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the University of Islamic Sciences (Karachi) method for Dhaka, widely used across Bangladesh.

faqItems.q: Is the prayer time in Dhaka different from Chittagong?
faqItems.a: Yes, Dhaka is west of Chittagong; the sun rises and sets a few minutes later in Dhaka than in Chittagong.

faqItems.q: When is the Bishwa Ijtema held?
faqItems.a: The Bishwa Ijtema is typically held in January or February each year on the banks of the Turag River on the outskirts of Dhaka.

istanbul.name: Istanbul
istanbul.insights: Istanbul is the bridge between East and West and was the seat of the Ottoman Caliphate for centuries. The city's skyline is defined by the majestic domes and slender minarets of the Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque. Istanbul's Islamic heritage is a unique blend of Byzantine grandeur and Ottoman elegance, serving as a global center of Islamic art, calligraphy, and history.
facts: The Blue Mosque is famous for the hand-painted blue tiles that adorn its interior walls and is the only mosque in Turkey with six minarets.
Hagia Sophia, originally a cathedral, served as a mosque for nearly 500 years and was restored as a working mosque in 2020.
Istanbul's Topkapi Palace houses the Sacred Relics of Islam, including the Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ mantle and sword.
The Suleymaniye Mosque, designed by the great architect Mimar Sinan, is one of the finest examples of Ottoman architecture.
Istanbul served as the capital of the Ottoman Empire from 1453 until 1922, during which it was the center of the Islamic world.
istanbul.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Istanbul is magical — the area between Sultanahmet and Hagia Sophia becomes a festival ground with religious book fairs, traditional music, and public iftars.

faqItems.q: Which method is used for Istanbul Namaz timings?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Diyanet Isleri Baskanligi (Turkey) method, the official standard for all mosques in the Republic of Turkey.

faqItems.q: Are these timings valid for both the European and Asian sides of Istanbul?
faqItems.a: Yes, but due to the city's vast size, there may be 1–2 minute difference between the westernmost and easternmost districts.

faqItems.q: When is the night of Laylat al-Qadr celebrated in Istanbul?
faqItems.a: Laylat al-Qadr is celebrated with great fervor in Istanbul's grand mosques, traditionally on the 27th night of Ramadan.

cairo.name: Cairo
cairo.insights: Cairo, the 'City of a Thousand Minarets', is the historic heart of Islamic intellectual life in the Arab world. Founded by the Fatimids in the 10th century, the city flourished under the Ayyubids and Mamluks, leaving behind a treasure trove of mosques, madrasas, and palaces. Al-Azhar, both a mosque and one of the world's oldest universities, remains the primary global authority for Sunni Islamic scholarship.
facts: Al-Azhar University in Cairo is the oldest degree-granting institution in Egypt and has been a global center of Islamic learning since 970 CE.
The Citadel of Saladin is a medieval Islamic fortification that houses the stunning Muhammad Ali Mosque (the Alabaster Mosque).
Islamic Cairo, a UNESCO World Heritage site, contains some of the best-preserved medieval Islamic architecture in the world.
The Mosque of Ibn Tulun, built in 879 CE, is one of the oldest mosques in Cairo and is famous for its unique spiral minaret.
Cairo's Khan el-Khalili bazaar has been a center of trade and artisan workshops since the 14th century.
cairo.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Cairo is famous for the 'Fanous' (colorful lanterns) that decorate every street, and the tradition of 'Mawa'ed el-Rahman' (tables of the Merciful) where free meals are served to all.

faqItems.q: Which method is used for Cairo prayer timings?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Egyptian General Authority of Survey method, which is the official standard for the Arab Republic of Egypt.

faqItems.q: Is the prayer time in Cairo different from Alexandria?
faqItems.a: Yes, Alexandria is west of Cairo; its prayer times typically occur 2–4 minutes later than in the capital.

faqItems.q: What is the significance of the Ramadan Cannon in Cairo?
faqItems.a: The firing of the cannon (Midfa al-Iftar) from the Cairo Citadel has a long tradition of signaling the time to break the fast, heard across the city.

abu-dhabi.name: Abu Dhabi
abu-dhabi.famousLandmark: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque – a masterpiece of modern Islamic architecture
abu-dhabi.insights: Abu Dhabi, the capital of the UAE, is home to one of the most stunning mosques in the world. The Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, with its 82 domes and 1,000 columns, serves as a global landmark of Islamic art and peaceful coexistence. The city combines heritage sites like Qasr Al Hosn with modern Islamic cultural centers, reflecting its commitment to preserving and sharing Islamic values.
facts: The Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque houses the world's largest hand-knotted carpet and one of the largest chandeliers in a mosque.
Abu Dhabi's Qasr Al Hosn is the oldest stone building in the city and contains a historic mosque that has served generations.
The city is a major center for Islamic finance and hosts numerous international conferences on Islamic culture and economy.
Abu Dhabi's Mary, Mother of Jesus Mosque (Masjid Maryam Um 'Issa) is famous for its name, symbolizing interfaith respect.
During Ramadan, the city's parks and public spaces host massive communal iftars organized by the Red Crescent.
abu-dhabi.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Abu Dhabi is marked by a serene atmosphere, with the Grand Mosque offering some of the most beautiful Taraweeh and Tahajjud prayers in the region.

faqItems.q: What method is used for Abu Dhabi prayer time calculations?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Umm al-Qura method for Abu Dhabi, consistent with the UAE's official prayer timings.

faqItems.q: Is prayer time in Abu Dhabi different from Dubai?
faqItems.a: Yes, Abu Dhabi is west of Dubai, so its prayer times occur approximately 3–4 minutes later than in Dubai.

faqItems.q: Can non-Muslims visit the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque during Ramadan?
faqItems.a: Yes, visiting hours are usually maintained for non-Muslims during Ramadan, though they are often restricted during prayer times and on Fridays.

jeddah.name: Jeddah
jeddah.famousLandmark: Al-Balad (Historic Jeddah) and the Floating Mosque
jeddah.insights: Jeddah has served as the 'Gateway to Mecca' for centuries, receiving millions of pilgrims by sea and air. The historic Al-Balad district, a UNESCO World Heritage site, is filled with ancient mosques and traditional coral-stone houses. Today, Jeddah is a vibrant coastal city where the iconic Floating Mosque (Masjid Al-Rahma) stands as a symbol of its enduring connection to the Red Sea and Islamic history.
facts: Al-Balad contains the Al-Shafi'i Mosque, one of the oldest and most important mosques in the city, dating back to the 13th century.
The Floating Mosque is built on pillars over the Red Sea and is a favorite spot for pilgrims to pray during sunset.
Jeddah is home to King Fahd's Fountain, the tallest of its kind in the world, often illuminated during Islamic holidays.
The city's historic gate, Bab Makkah, has seen millions of pilgrims pass through on their way to the holy city of Mecca.
Jeddah hosts the headquarters of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), making it a political hub for the Muslim world.
jeddah.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Jeddah is characterized by the 'Sahar' markets and the festive atmosphere in Al-Balad, where families gather to break fast by the sea.

faqItems.q: What calculation method is used for Jeddah prayer times?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Umm al-Qura University method, the official standard for all cities in Saudi Arabia.

faqItems.q: Is Jeddah's prayer time the same as Mecca?
faqItems.a: No, Jeddah is about 70km west of Mecca, so its prayer times typically occur 2–3 minutes later than in Mecca.

faqItems.q: When is the best time to visit Al-Balad during Ramadan?
faqItems.a: Al-Balad comes to life after Taraweeh prayer, with traditional markets and food stalls remaining active until the early hours of Sahur.

islamabad.name: Islamabad
islamabad.famousLandmark: Faisal Mosque – an iconic desert tent-inspired mosque
islamabad.insights: Islamabad, the purpose-built capital of Pakistan, is home to the Faisal Mosque, one of the most recognizable mosques in the world. Nestled at the foot of the Margalla Hills, the city's serene environment and modern planning make it a unique center for Islamic life. Islamabad is also a hub for national religious institutions and serves as a gateway to the historic Islamic sites of the Taxila and Potohar regions.
facts: Faisal Mosque was for several years the largest mosque in the world and can accommodate over 300,000 worshippers across its grounds.
The mosque was a gift from King Faisal of Saudi Arabia and features a unique architectural design without traditional domes.
Islamabad's Margalla Hills are home to the shrine of Bari Imam, a 17th-century Sufi saint and a major spiritual landmark.
The city's Planning Commission was designed with a focus on green spaces and natural beauty, earning it the title 'The Beautiful'.
Islamabad hosts the International Islamic University, attracting thousands of scholars from across the Muslim world.
islamabad.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Islamabad is peaceful and organized — the Faisal Mosque holds massive Taraweeh congregations that attract worshippers from across the Rawalpindi-Islamabad area.

faqItems.q: What method is used for Islamabad prayer time calculations?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the University of Islamic Sciences (Karachi) method for Islamabad, with 18° angles for Fajr and Isha.

faqItems.q: Is prayer time in Islamabad different from Rawalpindi?
faqItems.a: Due to their extreme proximity, the prayer times for Islamabad and Rawalpindi are virtually identical, usually within seconds of each other.

faqItems.q: What is the best place for Eid prayer in Islamabad?
faqItems.a: The Faisal Mosque is the most iconic venue for Eid prayers in the capital, though many choose the city's various sector-wise Eidgahs.

london.name: London
london.insights: London is one of the most diverse and vibrant Muslim hubs in the Western world. From the historic East London Mosque in Whitechapel to the iconic golden-domed Regent's Park Mosque, the city's Islamic presence is deeply woven into its cultural fabric. London's Muslim community, hailing from every corner of the globe, has created a unique British Islamic identity that is reflected in the city's architecture, cuisine, and public life.
facts: The East London Mosque is one of the oldest and largest mosques in the UK, serving as a major community and educational hub.
London Central Mosque, with its massive golden dome, was built on land donated by George VI in exchange for land in Cairo for an Anglican cathedral.
The city's Edgware Road and Whitechapel areas are famous centers for Middle Eastern and South Asian Islamic culture.
London has over 400 mosques and prayer rooms serving one of the most multi-ethnic Muslim populations in the world.
During the month of Ramadan, many of London's major landmarks and streets are decorated with festive lights to celebrate with the community.
london.ramadanNote: Ramadan in London features the 'Open Iftar' project, which hosts communal breaking of fast at iconic locations like Trafalgar Square and Wembley Stadium.

faqItems.q: What calculation method is used for London prayer times?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Muslim World League (MWL) method for London, with Fajr at 18° and Isha at 17°.

faqItems.q: How are prayer times handled during 'White Nights' in London summer?
faqItems.a: During peak summer at high latitudes like London, twilight may not disappear. In such cases, we follow the 'Nearest Latitude' or '1/7th of the night' rule as per local mosque guidelines.

faqItems.q: Where is the best place to find Halal food for Iftar in London?
faqItems.a: Streets like Edgware Road, Brick Lane, and the Green Street area in Newham offer hundreds of diverse Halal dining options for Iftar.

new-york.name: New York
new-york.famousLandmark: Islamic Cultural Center of New York (Manhattan)
new-york.insights: New York City is a true mosaic of the global Muslim Ummah. With mosques in all five boroughs, from the grand purpose-built centers in Manhattan and Queens to the storefront masjids of Brooklyn, the city reflects the incredible diversity of its residents. NYC Muslims have a long history, contributing to the city's social, professional, and cultural life for well over a century.
facts: The Islamic Cultural Center of New York in Upper East Side was the first purpose-built mosque in the city, established in 1991.
New York City has the largest Muslim population of any city in the United States, representing over 40 different nationalities.
The city's public school system officially recognizes Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha as holidays, a major milestone for the community.
Queens is home to some of the most diverse Muslim neighborhoods in the world, including Astoria and Richmond Hill.
The Muslim Day Parade, held annually in Manhattan since 1985, celebrates the community's heritage and contributions to the city.
new-york.ramadanNote: Ramadan in New York is a time of intense community activity — night prayers (Taraweeh) are held in community centers and gymnasiums across the city to accommodate large crowds.

faqItems.q: What calculation method is used for New York prayer times?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Islamic Society of North America (ISNA) method for NYC, with 15° angles for both Fajr and Isha.

faqItems.q: Are these timings valid for all five boroughs?
faqItems.a: Yes, while there may be a few seconds of difference between Staten Island and the Bronx, these timings are accurate for all of NYC and Jersey City.

faqItems.q: When is the Eid prayer in NYC?
faqItems.a: Large Eid prayers are often held in major venues like the Javits Center or public parks, usually starting between 7:30 AM and 9:00 AM.

toronto.name: Toronto
toronto.famousLandmark: Islamic Foundation of Toronto and Jami Mosque
toronto.insights: Toronto is the heart of the Canadian Muslim community and one of the most welcoming global cities for the Ummah. From the historic Jami Mosque (a former church) to the modern multi-service complexes of the GTA, Toronto's Muslims play an active role in all sectors of Canadian society. The city is famous for its multicultural 'Eid festivals' and its massive network of Islamic aid organizations.
facts: Jami Mosque on Boustead Ave is Toronto's oldest mosque, founded in 1968, and has served as a cornerstone for the community.
The Islamic Foundation of Toronto in Scarborough is one of the largest and most comprehensive Islamic centers in North America.
Toronto hosts the annual 'Reviving the Islamic Spirit' (RIS) convention, one of the largest Islamic gatherings in the West.
The city's diverse cuisines make it a global destination for Halal street food, from Somali and Afghan to Pakistani and Arab.
Nearly 8% of Toronto's population identifies as Muslim, making it one of the most concentrated Muslim communities in North America.
toronto.ramadanNote: During Ramadan, Toronto's mosques often host interfaith iftars, inviting the wider Canadian community to share in the spirit of the month.

faqItems.q: What calculation method is used for Toronto prayer times?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Islamic Society of North America (ISNA) method for Toronto, which is the standard for the majority of GTA mosques.

faqItems.q: Is the prayer time in Toronto the same as in Mississauga?
faqItems.a: Mississauga is just west of Toronto; prayer times typically occur 1–2 minutes later than in downtown Toronto.

faqItems.q: How does the high latitude affect Toronto's Isha time in summer?
faqItems.a: In summer, Isha time can be very late in Toronto. Many local mosques follow the 'Fixed Angle' or '1/7th Night' method to ensure reasonable prayer windows.

paris.name: Paris
paris.famousLandmark: Grande Mosquée de Paris – the oldest and largest mosque in mainland France
paris.insights: Paris has a long and complex relationship with Islam, centered around the beautiful Hispano-Moresque architecture of the Great Mosque of Paris. Built in the 1920s to honor Muslim soldiers, the mosque's tranquil gardens and stunning minaret are iconic features of the city. Today, the Muslim community in Paris and its suburbs (the Banlieues) is a vital part of the city's youthful energy and cultural diversity.
facts: The Great Mosque of Paris was built on the site of a former hospital and is famous for its green-tiled minaret and Moroccan-style mosaics.
During WWII, the Great Mosque served as a refuge for Jews escaping the Nazi occupation, providing them with falsified Muslim identities.
Paris and its surrounding region have the largest concentration of Muslims in Europe, with over 1.5 million residents.
The Institut du Monde Arabe (IMA) in the heart of Paris is a world-class cultural center celebrating Arab and Islamic heritage.
The neighborhood of Barbès in the 18th arrondissement is a major hub for North African Muslim culture and trade.
paris.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Paris is a time for family and charity — the teahouses inside the Great Mosque are popular spots for breaking fast with traditional North African pastries.

faqItems.q: Which method is used for Paris prayer timings?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Union des Organisations Islamiques de France (UOIF) method, which calculates Fajr and Isha at 12°.

faqItems.q: Are these timings valid for the Paris suburbs (Banlieue)?
faqItems.a: Yes, these timings cover the entire Île-de-France region including Saint-Denis, Argenteuil, and Nanterre with minimal variation.

faqItems.q: Can tourists visit the Great Mosque of Paris?
faqItems.a: Yes, part of the Great Mosque is open to tourists during the day, featuring a beautiful courtyard, a traditional cafe, and a hammam.

sydney.name: Sydney
sydney.famousLandmark: Lakemba Mosque (Masjid Ali Bin Abi Talib)
sydney.insights: Sydney is home to Australia's largest and oldest Muslim community. The suburb of Lakemba is the heart of Islamic life in the city, famous for its annual Ramadan Night Markets. From the grand Ottoman-style Auburn Gallipoli Mosque to the vibrant multi-ethnic masjids of the Western suburbs, Sydney's Muslims have built a flourishing community that contributes significantly to Australia's multicultural success.
facts: Lakemba Mosque is Australia's largest mosque and a major center for Islamic activities and community outreach.
The Auburn Gallipoli Mosque was built with an Ottoman architectural style, featuring materials and stones brought directly from Turkey.
Ramadan in Lakemba attracts over a quarter of a million visitors annually to its night markets, becoming a major Sydney cultural event.
Sydney's Muslim population is incredibly diverse, with large Lebanese, Turkish, South Asian, and Indonesian communities.
The first mosque in Sydney was established in Surry Hills in the early 20th century, marking the start of a permanent Islamic presence.
sydney.ramadanNote: During Ramadan, Haldon Street in Lakemba transforms into a massive open-air food festival after sunset, serving everything from camel burgers to Lebanese sweets.

faqItems.q: What calculation method is used for Sydney prayer times?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Muslim World League (MWL) method for Sydney, with 18° Fajr and 17° Isha angles.

faqItems.q: Does Sydney observe Daylight Saving Time for prayer calculations?
faqItems.a: Yes, our system automatically adjusts for Sydney's Daylight Saving Time (AEST/AEDT) to ensure your prayer schedule is always correct.

faqItems.q: Where is the largest Eid prayer in Sydney?
faqItems.a: The Lakemba Mosque traditionally hosts the largest Eid congregation in Australia, often requiring several shifts to accommodate the thousands of worshippers.

melbourne.name: Melbourne
melbourne.famousLandmark: Melbourne Grand Mosque and Islamic Museum of Australia
melbourne.insights: Melbourne is a major center for Islamic art and education in Australia. The city is unique for hosting the Islamic Museum of Australia, which showcases the history and contributions of Muslims to the nation. With diverse communities in areas like Broadmeadows and Tarneit, Melbourne's Islamic life is integrated into the city's reputation as a global cultural capital.
facts: The Melbourne Grand Mosque in Tarneit is one of the largest mega-centers for the community, established to serve the fast-growing Western suburbs.
Melbourne is home to the Islamic Museum of Australia, the first museum of its kind in the country, fostering intercultural dialogue.
The Australian Islamic Centre in Newport is a modern architectural masterpiece designed by the renowned Pritzker-winner Glenn Murcutt.
Victoria's Muslim community holds a 'Grand Iftar' at major venues like the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) to celebrate during Ramadan.
The city has a long history of Afghan cameliers who played a vital role in exploring the Australian outback during the 19th century.
melbourne.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Melbourne features 'Ramadan Nights' festivals in the Northern suburbs, where local bakeries and restaurants stay open late for Post-Taraweeh gatherings.

faqItems.q: What calculation method is used for Melbourne prayer times?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Muslim World League (MWL) method for Melbourne, which is the standard followed by the Islamic Council of Victoria.

faqItems.q: Is prayer time in Melbourne different from Sydney?
faqItems.a: Yes, Melbourne is south and west of Sydney; hence, the prayer times can differ by up to 10–20 minutes depending on the time of year.

faqItems.q: Can I visit the Islamic Museum of Australia?
faqItems.a: Yes, the museum is open to the general public and offers a fascinating look into Islamic heritage and its place in the Australian context.

moscow.name: Moscow
moscow.famousLandmark: Moscow Cathedral Mosque – one of the largest in Europe
moscow.insights: Moscow has one of the largest Muslim populations of any European city, with a history tied to the ancient Tatar communities and the broader Russian Federation. The magnificent Moscow Cathedral Mosque, with its striking golden dome, is the spiritual center for millions. During major holidays like Eid, the streets around the grand mosques fill with thousands of worshippers in a powerful display of faith.
facts: The Moscow Cathedral Mosque was rebuilt in 2015 and is one of the largest and most technically advanced mosques in Europe, with 6 floors.
Islam is recognized as one of Russia's four traditional religions, and Moscow has been a center for Tatar Muslim culture for centuries.
The city's 'Historical Mosque' in Zamoskvorechye dates back to the 18th century and is a preserved piece of Moscow's Islamic past.
Every year, Moscow holds a major 'Ramadan Tent' cultural festival near the Memorial Mosque at Poklonnaya Hill.
Halal food is widely available across Moscow, reflecting the city's multi-ethnic character and strong ties to Central Asia and the Caucasus.
moscow.ramadanNote: During Ramadan, the Grand Mosque of Moscow hosts large communal iftars for thousands of people, and several mosques organize nightly religious lectures.

faqItems.q: What calculation method is used for Moscow prayer times?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Muslim World League (MWL) method for Moscow, appropriate for the city's high latitude (55°N).

faqItems.q: How do long summer days affect fasting in Moscow?
faqItems.a: During summer Ramadan at 55°N, fasting hours can be very long (over 18 hours). Local scholars often provide specific fatwas for such conditions.

faqItems.q: Which is the main mosque in Moscow for Eid prayers?
faqItems.a: The Moscow Cathedral Mosque (near Prospect Mira) is the primary venue, attracting tens of thousands for the national televised Eid prayer.

berlin.name: Berlin
berlin.famousLandmark: Şehitlik Mosque - beautiful Ottoman-style mosque in Neukölln
berlin.insights: Berlin's Muslim community is a vital part of the city's modern identity, predominantly influenced by the Turkish guest-worker generation and more recent refugees. The Şehitlik Mosque, built with classic Ottoman architecture, is one of the city's most beloved landmarks. Berlin's Neukölln and Kreuzberg districts are vibrant centers of Islamic life, where the Adhan is a familiar sound in many community courtyards.
facts: The Şehitlik Mosque was built between 1999 and 2005 on the site of a historic Muslim cemetery dating back to the late 18th century.
Berlin is home to the 'House of One', a unique interfaith project where a mosque, a synagogue, and a church are being built under one roof.
The city's Mevlana Mosque and Omar Ibn al-Khattab Mosque are major community hubs for both worship and social welfare.
Nearly 10% of Berlin's population identifies as Muslim, representing a diverse background from Turkey, the Arab world, and beyond.
Berlin's Sonnenallee, also known as 'Arab Street', is famous for its vibrant community and excellent selection of traditional Halal food.
berlin.ramadanNote: Ramadan in Berlin is marked by long evening gatherings in Neukölln, where the community comes together to share iftar in the city's many restaurants and parks.

faqItems.q: Which method is used for Berlin prayer times?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Muslim World League (MWL) method for Berlin, with Fajr and Isha calculated at 18° and 17° respectively.

faqItems.q: Is prayer time in Berlin different from Munich?
faqItems.a: Yes, Berlin is much further north and east than Munich; summer days are longer, and sun-based prayer times differ significantly between the two.

faqItems.q: What is the best way to find a mosque in Berlin?
faqItems.a: Most districts in Berlin have multiple mosques; the Neukölln and Kreuzberg areas have the highest density, with several major Islamic centers.

madrid.name: Madrid
madrid.insights: Madrid's Islamic history is ancient; the city was founded by Emir Mohamed I in the 9th century and named 'Mayrit'. Today, the Madrid Central Mosque (Mezquita de Estrecho) serves as the primary hub for the city's growing Muslim community. Madrid preserves its Islamic roots in the remnants of its Arab walls and the Mudéjar architecture that continues to influence the aesthetics of the Spanish capital.
facts: Madrid Central Mosque, inaugurated in 1988, was the first purpose-built mosque in Madrid after the Reconquista era.
The city's name 'Madrid' is derived from the Arabic 'Majrit', meaning 'place of many springs' or water-channels.
Emir Mohamed I Park contains the remaining ruins of the original 9th-century Arab Wall that surrounded the Islamic citadel of Mayrit.
Madrid's Muslim community is incredibly diverse, with large Moroccan, Algerian, and Pakistani populations, alongside Spanish converts.
The Islamic Cultural Center of Madrid (Mezquita de la M-30) is one of the largest mosques in Europe and a major landmark for the community.
madrid.ramadanNote: During Ramadan, Madrid's mosques host public iftars, and the Lavapiés neighborhood becomes a lively spot for after-prayer social gatherings.

faqItems.q: What calculation method is used for Madrid Namaz timings?
faqItems.a: RuhVerse uses the Muslim World League (MWL) method for Madrid, which is the standard for most Islamic centers in Spain.

faqItems.q: Does Madrid observe Daylight Saving Time?
faqItems.a: Yes, our system automatically applies the DST adjustments for Central European Time (CET/CEST) used in Spain.

faqItems.q: Are there historic Islamic sites to visit in Madrid?
faqItems.a: While most of the city's Islamic buildings were lost, you can visit the ruins of the Arab wall and several Mudéjar-style towers in the old town.
